What to do

Keep long logs out of the chat

Models get less accurate as the input gets longer. Source: Chroma study

How to fix it →

How to fix it

Keep long test and build output out of the conversation by filtering it down to the errors first, or hand long logs to a subagent. → hooks (.claude/settings.json)

How to fix it

The rule was already in your instruction file, so make it checkable, keep the file under 200 lines, confirm it loads, and enforce must-never-break rules with a hook or deny rule, not emphasis. → CLAUDE.md, /context all, hooks, permissions.deny (.claude/settings.json)

Resuming after long breaks · $0.35 lost

Start a new session after a long break

After a break the cache is gone, and the whole chat is billed again. Source: Claude Code docs

Show what happened →

How to fix it

After a break of more than 5 minutes (1 hour on a subscription), start fresh with a short summary instead of continuing the old conversation. → /clear

Details
How often
4 times · $0.35 of the $5.36 spent (6.5%)
How sure
Measured

Sources

  • Official docs: Claude Code docs: How Claude Code uses prompt caching · 2026-11-22
    “Cached prefixes expire after a period of inactivity. Default TTL: one hour for the main conversation on a subscription within plan usage, five minutes otherwise.”
  • Official docs: Claude Code docs: Manage costs · 2026-11-22
    “Use /clear to start fresh when switching to unrelated work. Stale context wastes tokens on every subsequent message.”

Evidence against: /compact after the break does not avoid the cost: with the cache gone, the summary request reprocesses the history — Claude Code docs: How Claude Code uses prompt caching

Switching model mid-session · $0.58 lost

Pick the model before you start

Each model has its own cache, so a switch rereads the whole chat. Source: Several sources

Show what happened →

How to fix it

Claude CodePick the model, the effort level and the connected tools before you start, and open a new session when you want to change them. → /model, /clear

CodexPick the model and the effort level before you start, and open a new chat when you want to change them. → /model, /new
